- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.67), model underestimates; adjust upward modestly.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days), leading to overshoot; cap upward revisions after spike.
- Mean reversion bias: model often holds prices too high after recent peaks; apply downward correction if 3-5 days of high prices.
- Forecast horizon 30d: model tends to overestimate later periods (especially 15-30d) when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; reduce later-term forecasts.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings, model fails to capture volatility; smooth transitions with weighted average of recent sentiment.
- Avoid extrapolating sentiment trends beyond 3-5 days; sentiment decay should be applied to forecast weights.
